extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys/agents) drafting or prosecuting chemical, pharmaceutical, catalyst, and alloy patent applications (Korean practice)
extracted.subtask_short: patent examination for alloys and chemicals
extracted.subtask_description: Examination guideline for assessing patentability, sufficiency of disclosure, claim construction, novelty, inventive step, and added-matter issues for chemical and alloy inventions (polymorphs, enantiomers, catalysts, selection inventions, and alloy compositions). Focused on what must be stated in specification and how claims are to be construed and evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step for polymorphic (crystalline) forms
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention claiming a compound with a specific crystal form (polymorph) that differs from a prior-art crystal form is considered to have inventive step if it has a clearly different qualitative effect compared to the prior art, or if it has a clearly different quantitative effect compared to the prior art regardless of qualitative effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specification should state the effect clearly even if no comparative test data with the prior art are provided. If the claimed effect is doubtful, it must be proven concretely by submitting evidence such as comparative test data trusted by the applicant/patentee after filing date. (See Supreme Court verdict 2010HU2865.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification of microstructure/properties for inorganic compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: For inorganic compounds where name and formula are identical but microstructure (e.g., crystal form, unit surface area) differs, the subject matter cannot be specified by name/formula alone; specific property that helps expect the microstructure must be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if microstructure is not technically explained, if a specific property is stated in the specification, reviewers must evaluate the actual compound from that property. To determine inventive step for a preparation of an inorganic compound with specific feature, review of the specific property shall be included in the claim regardless of whether the property is explicitly stated in the claim. Determine whether it is reasonable to expect that the compound with the stated specific property can be produced by adopting/combining the components at the level of technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of product-by-use claims ('compound for ~')
rubrics_metrics.description: A chemical compound claim limited by wording 'for ~' (e.g., 'Chemical compound Z for Y') is construed as merely indicating utility and is read as the chemical compound without the use limitation (e.g., 'Chemical compound Z').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When 'for~' only indicates utility, the limitation does not create a distinct product-by-use; claim construction treats it as the compound per se.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of use-limited chemical compound claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If a chemical compound claimed with a use limitation is disclosed in the prior art (without the use limitation), the use-limited claim is deemed to lack novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Chemical compound Z for killing insects' is read as 'Chemical compound Z' and lacks novelty if 'Chemical compound Z' was already disclosed in prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step for selection inventions (selection from a genus)
rubrics_metrics.description: A selection invention claiming specific species selected from a generic prior-art disclosure is only inventive if the selected species all have different (qualitatively or quantitatively) effects from the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If specific compounds are merely selected from a wide range without demonstration of favorable or unexpected effects, the selection lacks inventive step. Conversely, if the selected compounds have unexpected favorable properties not disclosed or expected from prior art, inventive step may be acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of enantiomers relative to disclosed racemates
rubrics_metrics.description: If an enantiomer is specifically disclosed in the prior art when a racemate (racemic mixture) is disclosed, the enantiomer is considered to lack novelty. Also, if existence of the enantiomer can be derived from the prior-art disclosure by a person skilled in the art, it may be deemed disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even absent explicit data in the prior art, if the skilled person can find existence of an enantiomer from the prior disclosure or can easily carry out the invention based on then-current technology, novelty may be denied. (See Supreme Court verdicts cited.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step for enantiomer inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: If an enantiomer is not disclosed in detail in the prior art, its inventive step should be assessed by considering whether it exhibits extraordinary effects (chemical/physical/therapeutic) compared to the disclosed racemate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For use inventions of enantiomers, inventive step is recognized when prior art discloses only racemate without detailing enantiomer use, and the enantiomer shows different effects (qualitatively or quantitatively) compared to the racemate. It is sufficient that some effects differ; not all effects must differ. A difference cannot be denied merely because it could be found by simple tests. (See Supreme Court verdicts 2002HU1935, 2008HU736.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence standard for claimed enantiomer effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences in some effects of an enantiomer versus a disclosed racemate are sufficient to support inventive step; discoverability by simple tests does not negate inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if it is well known that a specific enantiomer has better medicinal effect, it may still be non-obvious that the claimed enantiomer has the better effect if prior publications did not make that specific enantiomer's use clear. Provide comparative data/evidence where effect is in doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty assessment for catalysts — composition and reaction context
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty of a catalyst cannot be determined without considering both the composition of the catalyst and the type of reaction in which the catalyst is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing novelty, examine composition and the reaction context together rather than composition alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step for catalysts used in different reactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a catalyst with identical or similar composition is disclosed, if the reaction in which the catalyst is used is not the same or the type differs, and the catalyst's effect (compared to no catalyst) is recognized for the claimed use, the invention may have inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare the claimed catalyst's effect in the intended reaction to the case without catalyst; recognize inventive step where reaction type differs and effect is shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step for catalysts with novel composition
rubrics_metrics.description: If no catalyst is disclosed with the same or similar composition for the intended reaction, the claimed catalyst is deemed to have inventive step by comparing its effect with the case without catalyst.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate catalytic effect relative to no catalyst to support inventive step when composition is novel for the reaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection between supported vs unsupported catalyst systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination of inventive step regarding the selection of supported or unsupported catalyst requires consideration of technical meaning stated in the specification or extraordinary effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporter (support) may be used for multiple purposes (produce effective catalyst, reduce cost, improve mechanical property, etc.). Unless technical meaning/effect of being supported vs unsupported is stated in the specification, the form/system difference is not automatically deemed to have specific differences. (See Patent Court verdict 2008HEO13732.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Alloy invention must specify alloying components and composition ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: Because alloy properties vary with element composition, an alloy invention must limit alloying elements and the composition range of each element to specify claims; structure, property, or use may be claim elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims only recite elements without composition ranges, the claim may fail to particularly point out the invention. Examples and exceptions are discussed (see sections on special cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Description requirements for numerical composition limitations (grounds & embodiments)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a numerical limitation to a composition range is stated in claims, the grounds and embodiment for that numerical limitation should be described in the specification, except where it is recognized the alloy can be specified and carried out easily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits of maximum and minimum must be clear; ambiguous terms not allowed. Describe reasons for numerical limits, significant effect across the whole range, and concrete reasons for synergy between components. Failure to disclose may force trial-and-error reproduction and fail Article 42(3) requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessity of test data and disclosure in alloy inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Because alloy effects are often unpredictable, the specification should disclose tests, embodiments, comparative examples and test results to prove the effect of the alloy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If test data are described, specify the target, method, requirements of the test, and technical effect not achieved by prior art so that a person skilled in the art can reproduce results. Case law citations provided where insufficient disclosure led to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embodiment representation requirement for alloy claims
rubrics_metrics.description: An embodiment that has a composition range consistent with and included in the composition range recited in the claims satisfies the disclosure requirement; at least one such embodiment is required to represent the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If embodiments omit essential alloying elements or include elements not recited in claims (except inevitable impurities), they do not represent the claimed invention. Specific content of each alloying element should be specified in embodiments; simply stating ranges without specific content may be insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity of claimed alloy effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Effects of an alloy invention should be specifically stated, including unique effects intended to be accomplished; abstract or subjective expressions are insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete statement of effects aids assessment of inventive step and sufficiency; vague claims about improved performance without quantified or otherwise concrete disclosure are inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturing method disclosure for alloy products
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claimed invention is a product alloy, the manufacturing method (melting, casting, heating, machining, plating, etc.) should be stated in detail in the specification so a person skilled in the art can reproduce the alloy, unless it is possible to manufacture the alloy by a normal method (in which case simple statement may suffice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different manufacturing approaches (smelting/refining vs machining/finishing) can be distinct inventions; lack of method detail can render patent rights unenforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim requirement — composition range limitation for alloy claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims for alloys should specify composition ranges of each alloying element; reciting only alloying elements without ranges normally fails to particularly point out the invention, except in special cases (homogeneous solid solutions, amorphous alloys, commercial alloys with known composition, or alloys in industrial standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When issuing rejection for lack of particularity regarding composition range, the examiner should state reasonable grounds in detail after reviewing the whole specification. Examples of acceptable claim phrasing are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recitation of allowable impurity ranges in alloy claims/specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Impurities should not be treated as elements of the alloy unless defined as impurities in the specification or known as impurities by common general knowledge; allowable ranges of impurities that significantly affect property or use should be specified (often upper limits like '0.3 wt% or less').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not necessary to limit every impurity, those that materially impact the alloy's properties should be clearly specified in the description and, where appropriate, in claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition of new matter — amendments adding numerical ranges/elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments that add new numerical ranges, add elements, or change composition ranges not disclosed in the original specification are deemed addition of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For alloy inventions (numerical-limitation inventions), adding alloying elements or composition ranges not in the original specification is typically new matter. Examples show when narrowing or expanding ranges constitutes new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: When amended numerical ranges are not considered new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: If the amended numerical range is obvious or inherent from the original disclosure and ordinary skill in the art, or if the amendment reduces a numerical limit that is supported by the original specification/embodiments, the amendment may not constitute addition of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: reducing an upper limit where that upper limit was already indicated as appropriate in the description or embodiments may be allowable; analyze whether the amended range is included in original matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (identity) criteria for alloy inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Identity of an alloy invention is determined by whether each element of the alloy is identical, the composition range and structure are considered identical, and whether the utility (property or use) is identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For manufacturing methods of alloys, determine identity of both the alloy and the manufacturing process. Utility may limit composition/structure when construed to specify the alloy invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method to determine identity when composition/structure overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: When claimed and prior-art alloys have identical composition and structure, they are substantially identical even if perceived properties differ; overlapping composition ranges may be considered identical, though a selected composition can be patentable if it has critical meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If composition and structure are identical, differences in perceived property or omitted use disclosures do not create novelty. Selection from a disclosed range may be patentable only where the selected sub-range has critical and demonstrable significance (e.g., unexpected technical effect). Case law examples illustrate these points.
